topic: Exact public SpeedRunner ASI replay implementation, nominal same-task replay binding, and remaining Figure-12 run-provenance gap

sources.observed_history: The public repository commit collection currently contains this initial commit only; GitHub releases are empty.

facts: The implementation explicitly ports the upstream ASI verification design and has allow_replay as a runtime switch.
Candidate induction mutates a deepcopy of the incoming codebook, not the live input object.
With allow_replay=false, proposed functions that pass static construction checks are immediately returned as the new codebook.
With allow_replay=true, a scripted test trajectory is required for every successful task shown to induction; missing tests cause return of the original codebook.
Each replay is executed on a fresh environment loaded by the same task_id, and must both satisfy env.check_solution and lexically invoke at least one newly added function.
Any failed replay returns the original codebook; all replays passing returns the candidate codebook. This is in-memory transactional commit/rollback.
sources.persistence_gap: The per-candidate test trajectories and replay results live in the local _ASIState and are not emitted as a structured durable manifest by ASISleep.update.

facts: ProblemLoader maps replay task_id back to the exact dataset record and constructs a fresh environment before env.reset(record).
A ScienceWorld record binds task_name and variation_idx; the record id embeds the family (when present), task name, and variation index.
make_data uses random.Random(seed=42) for reproducible sampling within the installed ScienceWorld task/split enumeration.
Thus replay is bound to the same nominal dataset record, but not to serialized simulator state bytes or an exact observation/state digest.

sources.boundary: The current public tree has no asi-gpt-t3.yaml for GPT non-replay task-3-only. Therefore the two currently named config files cannot themselves serve as a one-field matched run manifest for Figure 12, even though the paper states algorithmically that all other ASI components were left unchanged.

sources.claim: The public requirements specify 'scienceworld' without a version or artifact hash.

facts: The wake/sleep loop saves codebook snapshots and generic checkpoints into the run directory.
Although it passes a sleep_trace_path argument to the sleep strategy, ASISleep.update accepts and ignores unmatched kwargs and does not write its replay test trajectories/results to that path.
The repository gitignores /runs/, /logs, *.log, /data and output directories, so normal run logs/checkpoints are absent from the public Git tree.

sources.title: Heat transfer is stochastic
facts: Maintainer reproducer states that the same task, variation, simplification and command sequence could yield different outcomes: steam missing in 6/8 runs in one repetition and 4/8 in another, versus expected 0/8.
Comments explicitly note remaining simulator non-determinism and use of unordered Set structures.
The issue remained open until after the SpeedRunner paper date (2026-08-11) and initial public code release date (2026-08-14).
sources.scope_warning: This issue is a heat-transfer reproducer. It is evidence that nominal task+variation identity was not universally equivalent to exact simulator state/trajectory on the then-public ScienceWorld line; it is not evidence that SpeedRunner Figure-12 task 3 specifically encountered this bug.

sources.claim: PyPI's current stable ScienceWorld release is 1.2.3. An unpinned fresh install can therefore resolve differently from a version-specific evaluated environment; this observation does not identify what version the authors actually used.

derived_scope_limited_findings.claim: The exact public SpeedRunner implementation closes the earlier mechanism-byte gap for the ASI adaptation: allow_replay is an explicit receiver/admission switch over a deepcopy-staged candidate codebook, with no-replay committing after static checks and replay mode requiring same-record fresh-environment tests before all-pass commit. This matches the paper's qualitative replay-verification intervention much more closely than upstream ASI code alone.
derived_scope_limited_findings.scope: Exact current public adaptation bytes at the initial public release commit; still not a table/figure evaluated-run manifest.

derived_scope_limited_findings.claim: Same nominal ScienceWorld problem_id is weaker than same replay state. SpeedRunner's replay reconstructs a fresh environment from the same task_name+variation_idx record, while its public ScienceWorld dependency is unpinned and the benchmark maintained a known non-deterministic same-command reproducer through 2026-08-19. Therefore a scientific admission proof should bind exact environment artifact identity and either serialized/restorable state or repeated exact-replay equivalence, not only problem_id.
derived_scope_limited_findings.scope: General replay-proof provenance requirement. No claim that the Figure-12 task-3 runs were affected by the heat-transfer bug.

derived_scope_limited_findings.claim: The public SpeedRunner tree does not yet make Figure 12 numerically replayable: the only current GPT replay config is task-3-only, the current GPT non-replay config covers task families [3,4], run/log directories are ignored, ScienceWorld is unpinned, and the structured ASI sleep path does not persist candidate test trajectories/results. Thus the paper-level 'all other ASI components unchanged' statement remains the strongest matched-intervention evidence, while file-level run identity and exact plotted values remain unresolved.
derived_scope_limited_findings.scope: Absence on the observed initial public Git tree and release surface only; not a claim that the authors lacked internal run artifacts.

protocol_relation.composition_rule: A replay-verified admission packet should satisfy both transaction binding (candidate/pre-state/replay transcript/verifier/post-state) and environment replay equivalence (exact distribution/JAR + restorable-state or repeated exact-prefix evidence). A pass from a fresh nominally identical task instance is not, by itself, sufficient evidence of exact-state replay.
protocol_relation.new_validator: not added; this is a cross-protocol composition requirement rather than a new lifecycle state
